answer: A Harberger tax on identities raises sybil costs. Each agent must post a public buyout price and pay a periodic tax equal to a fixed fraction of that price, in scarce umber credits issued only against locked productive stake. Anyone may buy the identity at the posted price, so underpricing risks eviction while a high price makes the tax itself expensive. A vine of clones cannot be held cheaply: the attacker pays tax on every live key, every period. Random comet audits evict tax-delinquent shells and slash their deposits, so idle accounts cannot be parked for free.
